Title: Computer Systems Analysts
Task: Troubleshoot program and system malfunctions to restore normal functioning.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if kept advisory and read-only: the model accelerates triage by summarizing and clustering logs, explaining stack traces, mapping errors to known issues/KBs, generating safe checklists and rollback/runbooks, diffing configs, and drafting diagnostic commands or comms that humans verify. Typical gains: 15–40% faster MTTR on P1–P2 incidents and 0.5–3 hours saved on complex cases; even after verification/redaction effort, net savings are material (often hundreds to thousands of dollars per major incident) while preserving human-level quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect troubleshooting or remediation can cause outages, data loss, compliance violations, or security compromise. LLMs add risk via (a) plausible but wrong or outdated fixes that misconfigure systems; (b) prompt injection from logs/tickets/vendor pages steering unsafe advice or, in agentic setups, triggering harmful commands; (c) leakage of secrets/PII in logs, dumps, or configs when shared with non-compliant tools; (d) insecure workarounds (e.g., disabling auth/firewalls, overbroad permissions); and (e) attackers seeding telemetry or tickets to manipulate outputs or exfiltrate environment details. Compared to human-only workflows, LLM+expert increases operational/security risk materially—roughly 20–40% residual increase with strict read-only use, redaction, and mandatory human review; 1.5–3x if the system can execute commands or access internal networks. Experienced analysts can catch many issues, but subtle misinformation and leakage are hard to detect under incident pressure.

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

Typical savings: 1–5 minutes on routine tickets (approximately $0.50–$6 at $30–$70/hr) and 0.5–2 hours on complex incidents from automated evidence summarization and draft remediation plans (approximately $15–$140). At scale (e.g., 1,000–5,000 tickets/month), this can yield thousands of dollars in monthly savings and faster mean time to resolution while maintaining human-level quality if experts validate commands, use change control, and keep LLM output advisory.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety critical for system integrity and business continuity: bad guidance can cause outages, data loss, or weaken security. LLMs raise risk via incorrect troubleshooting steps or hallucinated commands, insecure configuration advice, and overconfident misdiagnosis that humans may not fully re-validate (automation bias). Handling tickets often exposes credentials, logs, or user PII, creating leakage risk if prompts or transcripts are stored or shared improperly. Attackers can socially engineer or prompt-inject through pasted logs or error messages to elicit unsafe actions (e.g., disabling EDR, running dangerous scripts). Toxic or unprofessional responses can harm user trust. Compared to human-only support, naive LLM use can raise the rate of unsafe or incorrect recommendations by roughly 10–25%; with strict SOPs, RBAC, sandbox testing, and mandatory human review before actions, residual incremental risk can be kept near 5–10%, though subtle misdiagnoses and privacy mistakes can still slip through.

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when kept advisory and verification-centric: LLMs can rapidly triage symptoms, generate precise clarifying questions, summarize multi-source logs into timelines, map error codes to likely causes, search/summarize vendor docs and change histories, propose safe diagnostic checklists, draft user communications, and translate instructions. Typical time savings of 20–50% on common tickets (e.g., Wi‑Fi/VPN/DNS issues), often 3–10 minutes on 10–20 minute tasks (~$2–$13 at $40–$80/hr), and ~10–30% on complex incidents via faster scoping, artifact summarization, and documentation (e.g., 30–90 minutes on a 5-hour incident). Quality can match expert-only outcomes if humans validate commands against authoritative sources, restrict models from executing changes, and use redaction plus access controls.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical for many organizations: bad troubleshooting advice can cause outages, data exposure, or weaken defenses. LLMs raise risk via (a) misinformation: hallucinated or outdated vendor commands, wrong root-cause attribution, and overconfident steps that break routing/DNS/VPN/firewall rules; (b) privacy: logs/configs can include PII, credentials, IPs/hostnames, and internal topology that may be exposed if shared with non-compliant systems; (c) security: suggestions to disable MFA, open ports/ACLs, or lower segmentation; if connected to tooling, prompt-injection from device banners/logs can cause unsafe actions or data exfiltration; (d) malicious misuse: attackers can use LLM-optimized prompts to socially engineer support or poison tickets/knowledge bases; and (e) discrimination: biased triage or language may lead to unequal prioritization. Compared to human-only workflows, use of LLMs without strict controls can increase the likelihood of a serious misstep by roughly 1.5–3x due to hallucinations and automation bias; with strong mitigations (read-only access, redaction of logs, stepwise approvals, and verification against runbooks/vendor docs), the incremental risk can be reduced to ~1.1–1.3x but not eliminated.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists
Task: Provide telephone support related to networking or connectivity issues.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used as a copilot: accelerate triage with dynamic decision trees, generate step-by-step scripts tailored to the user’s environment, summarize KB/vendor docs with citations, pattern-match logs/CLI output, map commands across vendors, provide clear user-facing explanations and multilingual support, and draft ticket notes. Typical savings are 2–6 minutes per routine connectivity call (approximately 15–30% handle-time; roughly $1–$5 at $20–$60/hr) and 10–20% on complex incidents via faster evidence organization—while maintaining expert-level quality if staff validate all commands against authoritative KB/change policy, require approval/rollback plans, and restrict the model from producing destructive steps or handling secrets.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect troubleshooting or configuration advice (e.g., DNS/DHCP changes, ACL/firewall rules, VPN settings) can prolong outages, reduce security posture, or cause data loss and compliance violations. LLMs may hallucinate commands, assume wrong OS/vendor/version, misread logs, or suggest disabling protections for diagnosis; such errors may not be evident until executed and can be hard to roll back remotely, amplifying automation bias under time pressure. Compared to human-only support, LLM-assisted workflows can increase the chance of a harmful step by roughly 1.5–3x if outputs are not strictly verified and change/rollback controls are weak; with strong guardrails (read-only suggestions, approved playbooks, mandatory verification, least-privilege tooling), residual risk can approach human-only levels. Added risks: leakage of sensitive configs/credentials in prompts (privacy), prompt/role injection via pasted device output or malicious callers (security), social-engineering amplification (misuse), and occasional unprofessional or biased language with users (toxicity/discrimination).

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward for drafting and tailoring materials: generate step-by-step guides, role-specific SOPs, policy summaries, translations, accessibility variants, quizzes, and simulated Q&A; triage common questions to reduce ticket load; convert vendor docs into org-specific quick starts. With expert review and test execution of procedures (approximately 0.5–2 hours per module), teams often save 20–50% of content development time and 10–30% on routine end-user support during rollouts. Typical savings: 3–10 hours per training package and 5–15 minutes per frequently asked issue (roughly hundreds to a few thousand USD of expert time), while maintaining human-validated quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy, Discrimination, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical in an organizational sense: incorrect or oversimplified training can lead to account lockouts, data loss, misconfigurations, insecure practices (e.g., disabling MFA), or users falling for phishing/social engineering. LLM-specific risks include confidently wrong how-to steps or policy interpretations; automation bias in learners; leakage of credentials/PII/logs pasted into the system; prompt injection via copied terminal output or web snippets; subtle bias in examples or accessibility of materials; and rare but possible toxic content in interactive Q&A. Compared to human-only training, LLM+expert moderately increases exposure by expanding scale and interactivity and by enabling tailored but potentially flawed guidance; with expert curation, dry-runs in a sandbox, and strict redaction/allowed-content policies, most errors are catchable, but nuanced security or environment-specific inaccuracies can slip through. Roughly a moderate risk increase (on the order of 10–30% more opportunities for harmful guidance if not carefully constrained), hence a risk rating of 3.

Title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators

gpt5_rewards_justifications: Meaningful but bounded gains when the model is used for read-only assistance: normalize and tag events, deduplicate, build timelines, cross-link tickets and assets, draft maintenance/repair narratives, highlight missing fields, and prepare auditor-ready summaries—while keeping immutable raw logs authoritative and requiring spot-checks. Typical savings: ~1–3 hours/week per admin on documentation and triage (≈$50–$300 at $50–$100/hr), or ~10–20 minutes per incident or maintenance action, without quality loss if outputs are verified and write access to canonical logs is prohibited.
gpt5_risks_types: Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: inaccurate or manipulated logs/records degrade incident response, compliance (e.g., audit trails/retention), and forensics, potentially causing data-breach impact, downtime, or legal exposure. Compared with human-only workflows, LLMs add failure modes—hallucinated or omitted entries, lossy summarization (timestamps/time zones/fields), format drift that breaks parsers, and automation bias that can let subtle inconsistencies pass. Privacy risk is elevated because logs often contain credentials/PII/keys; routing them through non-compliant systems can leak data. Security risk rises via prompt/log injection (attacker-controlled strings in logs influencing model behavior), weakened chain-of-custody if the model edits canonical records, and expanded attack surface if the model or its integrations have write access. Malicious actors can use LLMs to fabricate plausible maintenance records or to rationalize tampered logs. Many issues are hard to detect at scale because humans rarely re-verify every line against immutable sources.

Typical savings are around 3–10 hours per two-week sprint for a team lead managing 5–10 engineers (approximately $300–$1,500 at $100–$150/hr), plus 10–30 minutes per PR for first-pass review and summarization, while keeping quality if humans retain final approvals, use automated test/security gates, and run LLMs in compliant, access-controlled environments.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: errors in code-review judgments, task scoping, or workload allocation can propagate security bugs, outages, delays, or unfair treatment. Using LLMs raises risk via: (1) overconfident but wrong review comments or approvals, missing subtle correctness/security/performance issues; (2) leakage of source code, credentials, or performance data if models are used outside compliant environments; (3) exposure to prompt-injection or supply-chain attacks through model-integrated tooling tied to repos/CI; (4) biased task assignment or evaluation language that disadvantages protected groups; and (5) toxic or inappropriate tone in feedback. With disciplined controls (human-in-the-loop approvals, formal review checklists, SAST/DAST and tests as gates, access-controlled deployments, PII/IP redaction, and bias audits), most risks are catchable, but subtle bias and missed defects can still slip through. Relative to human-only workflows, naïve use can increase the likelihood of material review misses or privacy incidents by roughly 10–25%; with robust guardrails this can be limited to about 5–10% residual increase.

Using LLMs adds moderate incremental risk over human-only training because models can produce subtly incorrect or outdated guidance with high confidence, suggest insecure or noncompliant code, or leak proprietary code when prompts include internal context; trainees may over-trust AI and skip understanding. If the LLM is allowed to browse or run tools, prompt injection via pasted code/snippets and data exfiltration risks arise. Bias or toxic phrasing in examples can alienate learners. Most issues are detectable with expert review, static analysis/security checks on any code shown, and strict data-handling policies, but some subtle security and licensing mistakes can slip through, so residual risk is moderate.

Title: Web Developers

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward for routine installs/migrations: generate installation steps, config templates (vhosts, reverse proxy, TLS), systemd units, firewall rules, IaC snippets, and summarize vendor docs; assist troubleshooting by parsing logs/errors. With expert validation against official docs and automated tests/scanners, quality can match human-only while saving ~1–3 hours on a 3–6 hour setup (≈30–60%, ≈$100–$450 at $100–$150/hr). Savings shrink for highly customized or hardened builds where verification dominates, but remain positive if LLM outputs are treated as drafts and fully reviewed.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety critical: misconfigured HTTP servers/OS can expose services, enable RCE, data exfiltration, outages, or compliance violations. Using LLMs increases risk versus expert-only work via hallucinated/outdated directives (e.g., deprecated Apache/Nginx/TLS options), insecure defaults (weak ciphers, missing security headers, permissive directory/alias rules), subtle OS/network missteps (SELinux, iptables, systemd, cloud firewalls), and risky installation patterns (curl|bash, unverified repos). Agentic setups may be prompt-injected by untrusted docs/logs; privacy risk arises if configs/logs with secrets or host details are pasted into the model; attackers can solicit backdoored or vulnerable configs. Even with expert review, subtle misconfigs can pass smoke tests and be hard to detect. Compared to expert-only, LLM+human can raise the residual likelihood of security-relevant defects by roughly 10– 30% in internal audits and scanner findings due to hallucinations, outdated guidance, and automation bias; rigorous checklists, config linting/tests (nginx -t/apachectl -t), CIS/TLS benchmarks, staging, and secret scrubbing mitigate but don’t eliminate this uplift.

Compared to expert-only workflows, LLM+human can raise the likelihood of adopting insecure/outdated components or making erroneous tradeoffs by roughly 10–30% if outputs aren’t independently verified; with strict verification (primary docs, CVE/OWASP checks, license/legal review, threat modeling), residual risk can approach the human-only baseline but at added review cost.

gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs accelerate breadth and clarity of critique: propose alternative mechanics, surface edge cases, draft UX/accessibility/monetization checklists, summarize playtest notes, suggest A/B tests, and produce well-structured written feedback. With experts validating feasibility and policy alignment, teams can cut review/iteration cycles by ~20–40% (e.g., 2–6 hours per feature review, roughly $200–$900 at $100–$150/hr) while maintaining expert quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Discrimination, Toxicity, Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Not life-or-death, but feedback can cause significant organizational/user harm if it embeds biased or exclusionary tropes, uses toxic tone, recommends manipulative ‘dark patterns,’ or leaks confidential IP/playtest data. LLMs can hallucinate platform guidelines or engine limits and overstate claims from limited context; automation bias can amplify subtle errors across teams. Compared to human-only review, risk rises moderately due to scalable, confident mistakes and potential privacy/security leakage; most issues are catchable with expert review, DEI/accessibility checklists, and strict data handling, but subtle bias or inadvertent disclosure can slip through.

Title: Video Game Designers
Task: Create and manage documentation, production schedules, prototyping goals, and communication plans in collaboration with production staff.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when limited to assistive roles: draft and maintain specs, RFCs, and design docs from meeting notes; convert goals into backlogs, milestones, and dependency matrices; auto-generate standup summaries, risk registers, and comms; normalize formats across tools; create prototyping briefs and experiment plans; translate for cross-functional partners. With human verification for dates, scope, and dependencies, teams commonly save about 3–10 hours per milestone per producer/designer (approximately $300–$1,500 at $100–$150/hr), shorten cycle time, and reduce coordination churn while maintaining expert-level quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: incorrect timelines, scope, or change logs can cascade into missed milestones, contractual penalties, crunch, or budget overruns; flawed comms can harm morale or partner relations. LLMs add risk via hallucinated action items, mis-summarized decisions, loss of nuance in tradeoffs, and automation bias causing teams to accept faulty plans. Using non-compliant tools can leak confidential builds/roadmaps/IP; model or agent setups are vulnerable to prompt injection via pasted design docs or links; generated comms may contain biased or insensitive phrasing. Compared with human-only workflows, LLM+expert raises risk moderately (roughly 1.2–1.5x) unless mitigations are in place (secure environment, review checklists, data minimization, access controls, red-teaming). Many errors are catchable with producer review and traceability to sources, but subtle misprioritizations or quiet data leaks can be hard to detect.

Title: Video Game Designers

With experts validating factual claims and verifying against live builds, typical savings are about 15–30% per feedback round (e.g., 0.5–2 hours on a 2–6 hour review; roughly $50–$200 at $100/hr), while keeping quality equal to human-only processes.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Toxicity, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Not safety-critical; errors primarily affect product quality, schedules, or team dynamics rather than causing physical or societal harm. Using LLMs adds modest risk versus human-only review via: (a) misinformation or omissions about technical qualities/spec adherence that can misprioritize fixes and waste sprint capacity; (b) automation bias where staff over-trust plausible but wrong critiques; (c) privacy/IP exposure if unreleased assets or design docs are shared with noncompliant services; (d) biased or toxic phrasing that harms morale or fairness; and (e) potential prompt injection if the model ingests untrusted external text (e.g., community reports). Most issues are readily caught by experts through playtests, metrics, code/art reviews, and traceability to specs, and mitigated with human approval workflows, style constraints, red-teaming, and governed data handling; thus risk is low but non-zero.

gpt5_risks_types: Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Discrimination, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse

LLMs add risk via: (a) hallucinated or overconfident synthesis that misdirects design decisions; (b) biased summarization or survey generation that sidelines accessibility needs or minority cohorts; (c) amplification or generation of toxic language in prompts or tester communications; (d) prompt-injection or data exfiltration from untrusted tester text, logs, or bug reports; and (e) storage/processing of PII and confidential assets in noncompliant environments. Compared to human-only workflows, LLM+expert moderately increases incident surface (roughly 10–30% higher likelihood of privacy/security or interpretive errors before mitigations) and can hinder auditability if outputs lack source traceability. With de-identification, local/controlled processing, access controls, source-linked summaries, bias/QA checklists, and human sign-off, most failures are detectable and fixable.

Title: Video Game Designers

With strong editorial and compliance review (lore consistency, tone, ratings/TOS, and legal/IP checks), teams can maintain human-equivalent quality while reducing calendar time; for prestige, cinematic dialogue where heavy rewriting is required, savings are smaller but still material on ideation and alternate takes.
gpt5_risks_types: Toxicity, Discrimination, Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse

Compared with human-only workflows, introducing LLMs modestly increases the chance of problematic content slipping through if reviews are rushed—roughly a 10–25% relative increase in incident likelihood absent strong screening and editorial controls—but most problems are detectable with standard editorial QA, content filters, legal/IP checks, and style bibles.

Title: Video Game Designers

Experts then validate against design docs and compliance requirements. Typical savings are 20–50% of drafting time (approximately 2–6 hours for a mid-size plan), equating to roughly $100–$600 at $50–$100/hr, with potential 1–2 days saved on large plans—while maintaining quality if experts review and pilot the plan before execution.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Toxicity, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse

Using an LLM increases risk via: (1) planning errors or hallucinated coverage that omit edge cases or propose untestable steps; (2) privacy/security exposure if unreleased builds, internal docs, or tester data are shared with non-compliant services or exploited via prompt injection; (3) toxic or unprofessional phrasing in tester instructions/surveys; (4) biased inclusion/exclusion criteria that skew external cohorts and reduce validity; and (5) misuse, such as inadvertent leaks of spoilers or confidential mechanics. Relative to human-only workflows, naive LLM use can moderately increase risk (e.g., 1.5–2x likelihood of coverage gaps or data mishandling), but with expert review, redaction, access controls, and keeping outputs advisory, most issues are detectable and mitigable.

Title: Video Game Designers
Task: Provide test specifications to quality assurance staff.

Typical savings of 30–60% on test-planning for a feature (about 2–6 hours saved on a 4–12 hour task), i.e., roughly $80–$480 at $40–$80/hr; larger titles or sprints compound the gains without degrading quality when senior QA validates against official standards.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse

LLMs increase risk via hallucinated or outdated platform/TRC requirements, shallow or duplicated coverage, omission of edge cases, and overconfident prioritization (misinformation). Specs may also under-test accessibility or localization, embedding bias against certain players (discrimination). If leaked or abused, detailed specs can aid cheaters or modders in exploiting known weaknesses (misuse). Many errors are catchable if QA leads map specs to authoritative requirements, threat models, and coverage matrices, but subtle omissions are hard to detect until late testing.

Title: Web Administrators
Task: Monitor systems for intrusions or denial of service attacks, and report security breaches to appropriate personnel.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Meaningful efficiency mainly in Tier-1/Tier-2 workflows without ceding decisions: summarize and deduplicate alerts, extract entities/IOCs, build timelines, correlate artifacts to known TTPs, draft incident tickets and stakeholder updates, and propose next investigative steps or runbook snippets. With humans validating against authoritative telemetry and rules, typical savings ~20–40% on triage and reporting per incident (e.g., 15–60 minutes, roughly $20–$200 at $80–$200/hr), while maintaining human-quality outcomes; gains shrink for complex, multi-stage intrusions where verification dominates.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety-critical: missed or delayed detection or incorrect breach reporting can enable data exfiltration, outages, regulatory penalties, and reputational harm. LLM-specific risks include: (1) false negatives/positives and hallucinated correlations in noisy logs; (2) adversarial log/prompt-injection via attacker-crafted telemetry, tickets, or chat messages that steer the model or suppress alerts; (3) leakage of secrets/PII or sensitive configurations when logs are sent to the model; (4) outdated or non-local threat intel leading to wrong triage; (5) automation bias—analysts over-trust model summaries; (6) operational instability, latency, or cost DoS if attackers flood alerts to exhaust the model; (7) unsafe agentic actions if given command execution. Compared to human-only monitoring, advisory-only use with strict human verification increases residual risk slightly (~5–15% higher miss/latency risk); delegating triage/decisioning to the model can raise miss rates and time-to-detect materially (~25–50% in adversarial conditions). Mitigations (deterministic rules, sandboxing, model isolation, red-teaming, secret/PII scrubbing, and explicit human approval gates) are required to keep risk tolerable.

Title: Web Administrators
Task: Identify or document backup or recovery plans.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward for documentation and planning: LLMs can rapidly draft templates, RTO/RPO matrices, dependency inventories, runbooks/checklists, communications, and test plans, and consolidate scattered notes into coherent SOPs. With experts validating against authoritative vendor documentation and performing tabletop plus test restores, teams commonly reduce drafting time by 30–60% (≈2–8 hours per system plan; roughly $120–$960 at $60–$120/hr) while maintaining human-level quality, provided no secrets are shared and outputs pass formal change/control reviews.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety-critical: flawed backup/recovery plans (incorrect RPO/RTO, retention, encryption/immutability, off-site strategy, restore sequencing, or dependency mapping) can cause data loss, extended outages, and regulatory or contractual breaches. LLM use increases risk via plausible but incorrect or outdated vendor-specific instructions; omissions (e.g., application-consistent backups, key/credential backup, log chain integrity, dependency ordering, and access controls); and automation bias leading to under-review. Security/privacy risks arise if staff paste configs, credentials, or topology into prompts that may be logged or intercepted; agentic setups face prompt-injection and data-exfiltration risks; generated docs can leak internal architecture useful to attackers. Compared to expert-only drafting, the combined setup can raise the odds of a critical omission or sensitive data exposure by roughly 1.5–3x without strict controls, though thorough SME review and restore testing can catch many issues.

Title: Web Administrators

With experts performing dry-runs, least-privilege reviews, and periodic test restores, typical savings are ~10–30% on setup and documentation (e.g., 3–10 hours on a 20–40 hour DR/backups task, roughly $300–$2,000 at $100–$200/hr) and ~0.5–2 hours/month in maintenance, while maintaining quality. Net gains depend on strict validation (automated restore tests, checksum/point-in-time recovery verification) which absorb part of the time saved.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: errors can cause irreversible data loss, prolonged outages, or regulatory violations. Security/privacy risks include leaking credentials or PII when sharing configs or dumps with the model; generating overbroad IAM policies; and prompt-injection or tool misuse leading to execution of harmful commands if the model is granted shell/cloud access. Failures are often undetected until a real disaster or test-restore, making them hard to catch. Compared to human-only workflows, using LLMs (even with expert oversight) can raise the probability of subtle, latent misconfigurations by ~20–80% if outputs aren’t rigorously validated via test restores and audits; granting the model direct execution or access can push risk much higher. Attackers may also weaponize LLM assistance to script exfiltration or disable backups.

Title: Web Administrators

gpt5_rewards_justifications: Rewards are moderate when kept advisory: faster triage and diagnosis (log summarization, mapping error messages to likely root causes), generating config snippets, scripts, Infrastructure-as-Code diffs, and step-by-step runbooks; drafting incident comms and postmortems. With human validation and staging, typical savings are ~20–40% on routine fixes (about 0.5–2 hours per incident, roughly $50–$240 at $100–$120/hr). For complex incidents, verification overhead limits gains. Quality can match human baseline if all changes pass tests, security review, and change approval.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect fixes or recommendations can cause outages, data corruption, or expose systems and user data. LLMs can hallucinate commands/configs (e.g., disabling auth, overly broad CORS, permissive file permissions), misread logs, or omit edge cases edge cases, leading to insecure workarounds or brittle fixes. Sharing logs/configs with the model can leak secrets or PII; agentic integrations that read external content (tickets, logs, webpages) risk prompt-injection or adversarial instructions. If the model can write to repos or run commands, a single bad suggestion can propagate via CI/CD. Experts can catch many issues with staging, peer review, automated tests, and change controls, but subtle security regressions and availability risks can slip under time pressure. Relative to human-only workflows, using LLM-assisted suggestions raises residual risk roughly 10–30% when outputs are manually applied under normal reviews; granting the model execution/write access can push risk much higher, hence the high rating.

Title: Web Administrators

Experts must validate against authoritative sources and test in staging, which limits gains. With human approval gates, metric cross-checks, redaction, and role-based distribution lists, quality can match human-only while reducing effort. Typical savings: approximately 2–6 hours to draft the initial communication plan; 20–60 minutes per weekly status package; 5–10 minutes per daily update. Across a mid-size project this can save roughly 5–15 hours/month (approximately $400–$2,100 at $80–$140/hr), plus faster stakeholder response times.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination, Toxicity
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety critical: Yes (organizational and stakeholder harm). A faulty communication plan or inaccurate updates can trigger schedule slippage, compliance breaches, outages, or reputational damage. LLM-specific risks: (1) Misinformation—confident but wrong status, dates, or commitments due to misreading source docs or hallucination; automation bias can let errors propagate at scale. (2) Privacy—leakage of sensitive project data, credentials, or PII when drafting or summarizing tickets, logs, or vendor contracts. (3) Security—prompt injection or data exfiltration if the model is connected to project tools; misaddressed or overly broad distribution of messages. (4) Malicious misuse—mass emailing, persuasive but misleading comms, or phishing-like messages if access is compromised. (5) Discrimination—toxic or biased language that marginalizes stakeholders (e.g., excluding certain teams/time zones). (6) Toxicity—unprofessional tone in escalations or incident comms. Compared to human-only workflows, the combined LLM+expert setup can increase risk mainly via harder-to-detect subtle inaccuracies and privacy slip-ups; with strong gating (human-in-the-loop approvals, source-of-truth checks, redaction, least-privilege access) residual risk is moderate. Roughly a 20–40% higher risk than human-only if controls are weak; near parity with robust controls, but privacy/security incidents are hard to fully remediate.

Title: Information Technology Project Managers

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High rewards when the model drafts and the expert verifies: rapid decomposition from goals/requirements into tasks/subtasks, reusable templates by domain, auto-generated milestones, RACI suggestions, dependency and risk checklists, and quick refactoring as scope changes; also mapping to backlog items and producing stakeholder-friendly views. With expert validation (requirements traceability, architecture/security/compliance reviews, and estimate sanity checks), teams typically save 30–60% of initial WBS drafting time and 20–40% on updates. For a 10–20 hour WBS effort, this is about 3–10 hours saved (≈$300–$2,000 at $100–$200/hr) while maintaining human-expert quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical (organizational): a flawed WBS can omit compliance/security tasks, misorder dependencies, or under-scope work, leading to outages, cost/schedule overruns, audit findings, or contractual penalties. Using LLMs raises risk via plausible-but-wrong decompositions, outdated or hallucinated regulatory steps, hidden automation bias, and weak traceability to requirements. If fed sensitive specs or tickets, privacy/security risks rise (data leakage, prompt-injection from project docs, or unauthorized tool actions in agentic setups). Discrimination risk is lower but possible if role/task assignments reflect biased patterns. Relative to human-only, LLM+expert workflows increase the probability of scope/dependency/compliance errors by roughly 10–30% unless mitigated with SME reviews, requirement traceability, and governance (e.g., data minimization, approved templates, and red-teaming). Most issues are detectable with structured reviews, but subtle omissions can slip through, warranting a moderate risk rating.

Title: Information Technology Project Managers
Task: Monitor the performance of project team members, providing and documenting performance feedback.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when LLMs are used for drafting and organization, not final judgment: aggregate artifacts (tickets/PRs/OKRs) into timelines, map outcomes to competencies, propose SMART goals, adjust tone, translate, and generate consistent documentation. With expert verification and evidence links, teams commonly save 30–90 minutes per review (approximately $35–$225 at $70–$150/hr) while maintaining human-quality outcomes; complex cases may see smaller gains due to verification overhead.
gpt5_risks_types: Discrimination, Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety-critical because performance feedback affects compensation, promotion, termination, morale, and legal exposure. Using LLMs introduces moderate additional risk via biased or inconsistent language, hallucinated or misattributed achievements, automation bias, and overconfident summaries from incomplete or noisy sources (tickets, commits, standups). Privacy and security risks arise if employee PII or sensitive project data are processed outside compliant boundaries or via vulnerable integrations; prompt injection or data poisoning in source docs can skew summaries. Toxic or overly harsh phrasing can create hostile-work-environment claims. Compared to human-only reviews, unmanaged LLM use moderately increases risk (roughly 1.5–2x likelihood of materially biased, privacy-noncompliant, or inaccurate feedback), though many issues are catchable by requiring human verification against evidence, standardized rubrics, bias/language checks, and HR/legal review; subtle bias or inadvertent disclosure can still slip through.

Title: Information Technology Project Managers
Task: Coordinate recruitment or selection of project personnel.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High rewards when applied to operations rather than final judgment: draft role descriptions and outreach, summarize resumes into structured skill matrices, generate interview guides and scoring rubrics, draft candidate communications, and surface gaps or follow-up questions—then have humans verify against source resumes and assessments. Typical savings ~5–12 hours per role for an IT PM team (at ~$60–$120/hr = ~$300–$1,400), plus 1–3 days faster cycle time, with comparable quality if final screening and hiring decisions are made by humans using validated rubrics, reference checks, and bias/privacy reviews.
gpt5_risks_types: Discrimination, Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This coordination/selection task is safety-critical: biased or erroneous selection can cause material harm to candidates (fairness, employment) and to the organization (legal, reputational, project failure). Adding LLMs increases exposure vs human-only processes through overconfident screening, hidden representational bias, mishandling PII, insecure prompts or resume attachments that lead to data exfiltration or manipulation, and susceptibility to AI-crafted resumes or deepfake interviews. With strong controls—keep model output advisory, use structured rubrics, verify against source documents, log rationale, and use privacy-preserving data handling—many errors are catchable, but subtle disparate impact and compliance gaps can evade detection. Net incremental risk vs human-only is moderate (~15–35% higher likelihood of biased or privacy-noncompliant handling without safeguards; ~5–15% with safeguards).

Title: Information Technology Project Managers
Task: Assign duties, responsibilities, and spans of authority to project personnel.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward on the coordination/documentation workload: draft RACI/authority matrices, propose staffing options from skill inventories, generate role descriptions and decision rights, flag overlaps/gaps, balance workloads, and draft comms/approvals. When PMs validate against policy and stakeholder inputs, quality can match human-only. Typical savings of 2–6 hours per medium project (roughly $140–$900 at $70–$150/hr) and 10–20% faster assignment cycle time; larger gains on complex programs due to faster scenario exploration and more consistent documentation.
gpt5_risks_types: Discrimination, Privacy, Security, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This is safety-critical at the organizational level: misassigned duties or spans of authority can enable unauthorized decisions or access, create compliance or audit failures, and cause reputational and legal harm. LLM involvement increases risk versus human-only by introducing plausible but incorrect role mappings, biased or stereotyped allocations (e.g., by gender or seniority), outdated or hallucinated policy guidance, leakage of employee PII, and susceptibility to prompt-injection from pasted artifacts; if connected to ticketing/IAM, agentic errors could over-provision privileges. Automation bias can hide these errors. With the LLM kept advisory and human experts validating against org policy, segregation-of-duties, and approval workflows, most errors are catchable but not trivial to detect; mitigation requires bias checks, SoD/least-privilege reviews, audit trails, and privacy-safe data handling.

Title: Information Technology Project Managers
Task: Negotiate with project stakeholders or suppliers to obtain resources or materials.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if kept to preparation and analysis, not autonomous committing: draft negotiation briefs and email templates, generate counterarguments and concession strategies, summarize and compare terms across vendors, extract clauses into checklists, create issue lists and follow-up questions, simulate role-play, and translate communications. With expert verification and legal/procurement review, quality can match human-only outcomes while cutting prep/communication time by about 15–30% (approximately 3–15 hours on a mid-size negotiation), yielding roughly $300–$2,000 in labor savings at $100–$150/hr and faster cycle times.

gpt5_risks_justifications: This task can be safety-critical at the organizational level: unfavorable or noncompliant terms, IP or data handling mistakes, or inadvertent commitments can create material financial, legal, and reputational harm. LLMs raise risk by hallucinating or omitting key details in proposals/SLAs/SOWs, misrepresenting benchmarks, and inducing automation bias; by leaking confidential pricing, roadmaps, or PII when used outside compliant environments; by being vulnerable to prompt-injection or manipulated RFP text; and by introducing biased or unprofessional language that can breach fairness or procurement norms. Compared to human-only workflows, using LLMs with expert oversight can increase the probability of a material negotiation error or confidentiality lapse by roughly 10–30% absent controls; with mitigations (approved/privacy-preserving use, traceable citations to source docs, line-by-line verification, and legal/procurement review; no autonomous commitments), residual added risk is reduced but not eliminated.
